source: NCERT Class XI, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 1), Ch. 8 (Some Aspects of Indo-Islamic Architecture).

sections.heading: 1. Indo-Islamic Architecture — Character
points: From the **13th century**, a new style emerged blending **Islamic** features (arch, dome, minaret, calligraphy, geometric/arabesque designs) with **Indian** craftsmanship and motifs.
Islamic buildings avoided living forms → used **calligraphy, geometry and floral (arabesque)** decoration.
Key techniques: the **true arch and dome** (on squinches/pendentives), and later the **Charbagh (four-part garden)**.

sections.heading: 2. Building Types
points: **Mosque (masjid)** — courtyard, prayer hall, mihrab (facing Mecca), minbar; **Jama Masjid** = congregational mosque.
**Tomb (maqbara)** — often set in a garden (Charbagh).
Also **forts, palaces, sarais, gardens, minars, step-wells**.
Materials: stone (sandstone, marble), and decorative **inlay (pietra dura), tilework, jaali (lattice screens)**.

sections.heading: 3. Dynastic Phases
points: **Delhi Sultanate:** **Qutub Minar** and **Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque** (Delhi); Alai Darwaza (first true dome — Khalji); Tughlaq (austere, sloping walls); Lodi tombs.
**Provincial styles:** Bengal, Jaunpur, Malwa (Mandu), Gujarat, Bijapur (**Gol Gumbaz** — huge dome).
**Mughal architecture** — the grand climax.

sections.heading: 4. Mughal and Later
points: **Mughals:** Humayun's Tomb (first great Charbagh tomb); **Akbar** — **Fatehpur Sikri** (Buland Darwaza), Agra Fort; **Shah Jahan** — the **Taj Mahal (Agra)**, Red Fort and Jama Masjid (Delhi) — peak of marble, pietra dura.
The **Taj Mahal** (white marble, Charbagh, symmetry) is the finest example, built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal.
Regional/later styles influenced Rajput and Sikh architecture too.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Indo-Islamic features: true arch, dome, minaret, calligraphy, arabesque, Charbagh garden.
Qutub Minar + Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque = Delhi Sultanate (earliest).
Alai Darwaza = first true dome (Khalji); Gol Gumbaz (Bijapur) = huge dome.
Fatehpur Sikri, Buland Darwaza = Akbar; Taj Mahal, Red Fort = Shah Jahan.
Taj Mahal = white marble, Charbagh, pietra dura (built for Mumtaz Mahal).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Charbagh** = a four-part garden layout (Mughal tombs).
The **Alai Darwaza** (Khalji) has the **first true dome** in India.
The **Taj Mahal** was built by **Shah Jahan** for **Mumtaz Mahal**.
**Pietra dura** = stone inlay decoration (perfected under Shah Jahan).
